name: Unbound Method assignment requires callable-kind validation

input.source_text: class A { public fun f(x: Integer) -> Integer { x } } module M { public fun run() -> Object { let m = Reflection::Class.method(A, :f); let rejected = try { let bad: Closure<(Integer) -> Integer> = m; bad } catch e { e }; let bound: BoundMethod<(Integer) -> Integer> = m.bind(A.new()); [rejected, bound.class_name] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C094 reifies callable KIND, so `Closure<S>` types a Closure and `BoundMethod<S>` types a BoundMethod, and C039 makes an unbound Method a reflective definition object rather than an ordinary callable. Assigning one to a callable annotation was silently ACCEPTED because every generic annotation answered admits-everything; it now fails, and `Method#bind` supplies the explicit binding C039 requires, which produces a BoundMethod that only the BoundMethod kind admits. The binding pairs the RETAINED Method with the receiver rather than re-dispatching its selector, which would select whatever the current MRO resolves instead. The SIGNATURE half stays a static concern: C096 checks it at the call site rather than by variance between callable Types.
